1.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner as well as learned Additional Government Advocate,
representing the respondent ? State, and perused the entire file.
2.

By way of this petition under Section 482 CrPC, the petitioner has prayed for quashing of the orders dated 07.06.2018 and 10.12.2018 passed by the Special Judge (Prevention of Corruption Act)
Varanasi in Special Trial No.12 of 2012, under Sections 193, 218, 409, 420, 467, 468, 471, 477A and 120-B IPC read with Sections 13(2)/13(1) Prevention of Corruption Act, arising out of Case Crime No.0222 of 2006, Police Station Kotwali Chandauli, District Chandauli and the Special Judge be directed to consider and dispose of the discharge application.
3. This is second petition filed by the petitioner.

sentences.text: 4. This Court, initially granted an interim order on 11.05.2012.

The said petition was, however,
dismissed on 12.05.2016 for non-prosecution.
Thereafter, the application for recall ofthe said application was allowed vide order dated 13.01.2017 and the Petition No.16284 of 2012 was restored to its original number.

On the same day, this Court found that there was no ground to entertain the petition under Section 482 CrPC and the same was rejected with liberty to the petitioner to move an appropriate application before the Court concerned for discharge.

It is evident that even on the same day, the ground of the petitioner having been discharged in the disciplinary proceeding was available, which was not entertained by this Court and the petition was rejected with liberty to file a discharge application.

In the meantime, the petitioner had filed another petition under Section 482 No.14126 of 2018 on the ground that the discharge application filed by the petitioner was pending which had not been decided and this Court might direct to expedite hearing of the case and for decision on the discharge application.

The said petition was disposed of vide order dated 24.04.2018 with a direction to the learned trial Court to expedite the hearing of the discharge application and decide the same, preferably within a period of two weeks and should frame charge accordingly, if so required.

5. After the said order was passed by this Court, the discharge application filed by the petitioner was taken up for hearing and the same was rejected vide detailed order dated 07.06.2018 and, thereafter non-bailable warrants of arrests were issued against the petitioner and co-accused vide order dated 07.01.2018, which are impugned in the present petition.
The trial Court has found that there is more than prima facie case available against the petitioner and, therefore, the petitioner cannot be discharged.

6. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant submits that the accused-applicant has been exonerated in the disciplinary proceeding vide order dated 25.04.2011 in respect of making payment of Rs.13,512/- on the basis of forged documents prepared.
7. It is settled law that outcome of the disciplinary proceedings is based on preponderance of probability, however, in criminal proceeding the charge has to be proved beyond reasonable doubt.
The judgement of the Supreme Court reported in 2011 (3) SCC 581 (Radheyshyam Kejriwal Vs. State of West Bengal and another) has no relevance in the present case.

entities.text: 2011 (3) SCC 581 (Radheyshyam Kejriwal Vs. State of West Bengal and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In adjudication proceeding, it is the trained judicial mind which is not less than the Sessions Judge who adjudicates the trial proceeding and appreciate the evidences and therefore, it was held that if in adjudication proceeding, the accused is exonerated on merit, it would not be appropriate to continue with the proceedings in respect of the substantive offences for the same charges.

In disciplinary proceedings,
the finding is based on preponderance of probabilities whereas in criminal proceedings the guilt is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt and therefore, the finding of disciplinary authority can never be binding upon the criminal court, however, it may be correct vice-verse.
8. In view thereof, I do not find any substance in the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

The impugned order, rejecting the discharge application, has been passed, taking into consideration the law and the facts & circumstances of the case which does not require any Shiv Murat vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18300500/
2 interference by this Court in exercise of jurisdiction under Section 482 CrPC.

sentences.text: Therefore, the present petition is hereby dismissed.

However, it is provided that if the petitioner surrenders before the trial Court within a period of 10 days from today and move application for regular bail, the same should be consiered and decided expeditiously, in accordance with law.
[D.K. SINGH, J.]
